pattern: Myth vs fact carousel built on the 'Why diets don't work / Žiadne zázračné diéty' hook seen across TikTok and Meta ads, remade around doctor-led care and the persona's objections
why: The 'tried every diet' pain stops busy professionals, and each myth answers one real objection (real doctor, travel, price, follow-up), so every swipe resolves a doubt.

findings.message: Confirm the doctor in blur-doctor.jpg is unidentifiable or has given written consent; otherwise remove the face or add a clear dramatization label.
Check with the operator that the questionnaire time and the cancel-anytime terms are accurate, since operational claims must be true.

slides.issues: Strong, believable lifestyle photo with natural light and no visible AI tells. Headline is big and readable over the grey wall. The body line is small and sits close to the woman's head, so it loses punch at phone size. The hook is relatable, but 'a nič?' is a soft payoff. A sharper tension line or a bigger body line would help.

The real a.clinic site is clearly shown on the phone, which satisfies the product gate. The phone mockup over a blurred background reads more like an ad template than a creator post. The on-screen site says '20 minút' while slide 6 says 'asi 10 minút', so align the claims. The fact text is fine, though a bit dense.

Cozy evening home scene that reads authentic. Text sits on a dark gradient and is readable. 'Slovensku' orphans onto its own line, so rebalance the line breaks. The laptop screen is blank and dark. Showing the a.clinic questionnaire on it would reinforce the product.

Real-looking pharmacy street shot, and the green cross is recognizable. The blue highlight on 'stojí,' includes the comma, which looks sloppy. The image ties to pharmacy pickup rather than price transparency, so the visual-message fit is only partial. Body text over the busy storefront is borderline, so strengthen the gradient.

The subject's head is cropped at the top edge, which feels like an accidental crop. The figure is mostly covered by text, and the barefoot standing pose feels stocky. The visual does not clearly communicate an ongoing care team.

final.notes: The gate passes: the real a.clinic site appears on a phone on slide 2, and slide 6 carries the CTA with a.clinic. The myth/fact structure is clear, and the type system is consistent and legible. Main fixes: 1. Remove the blue circle placeholder on slide 6 and use a natural, brighter image, ideally with the real questionnaire on the phone. 2. Reconcile the '20 minút' on the site screenshot with 'asi 10 minút' in the CTA. 3. Recrop slide 5 so the head is in frame. 4. Fix the highlighted comma on slide 4 and the orphan word on slide 3. 5. Consider showing the product again on slide 3, using the laptop screen. Slides 2 to 5 have moderate hooks, so a more surprising fact line per myth would lift swipe-through.

The laptop screen is empty and from behind, so it misses a chance to show the consultation or questionnaire. There is an orphan word, 'nejde'. The body copy is long and wraps awkwardly ('na / Slovensku').

The pharmacy storefront looks real, but the image illustrates picking up medicine rather than price transparency, which is the actual myth. The headline sits over the walking woman's body, which feels cluttered. There is an orphan, 'neskôr'. The comma after 'stojí' in the highlight looks odd.

The subject's head is cropped at the top of the frame, which looks like an accident rather than a choice. The headline covers her torso. The phone call works for 'the care team calls you', but the composition is weak and the shot reads slightly staged.
